fine_trace.code: HashTable *values = php_fgetcsv(NULL, delim, enc, esc, ZSTR_LEN(str), ZSTR_VAL(str));
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled CSV string ("y") and escape character ("\0", a NUL byte) are passed into php_fgetcsv with stream=NULL; buf points at the NUL-terminated string and buf_len=1, so the byte right after the data is the string terminator.
For input "y" there are no trailing \r\n bytes, so limit = buf+1, i.e. limit points exactly at the NUL terminator that terminates the string.
inc_len is computed as 1 for the leading enclosure byte 'y' at bptr=buf.
The first byte 'y' equals the enclosure character 'y', so the enclosure-delimited field parser (2A) is entered.
bptr is advanced past the opening enclosure to buf+1, which is the NUL terminator; hunk_begin is set to the same position.

fine_trace.code: } else if (escape_char != PHP_CSV_NO_ESCAPE && *bptr == escape_char) { state = 1; } bptr++;
fine_trace.note: On the first loop iteration inc_len is still 1 but bptr already points at the NUL terminator; because escape_char is also NUL, *bptr == escape_char sets state=1 and bptr is incremented to buf+2 = limit+1, walking one byte past limit.
With bptr at limit+1 and inc_len now 0, case 0/state 1 copies the hunk and sets hunk_begin = bptr = limit+1; the fallthrough into case 0/state 0 reaches the stream==NULL branch.
Because bptr (limit+1) is past limit, bptr is decremented back to limit, but hunk_begin stays at limit+1; the invariant bptr >= hunk_begin (non-negative copy length) is broken.
At quit_loop_3 the copy length bptr - hunk_begin evaluates to -1 (converted to SIZE_MAX), so memcpy receives a negative size and ASAN reports negative-size-param / glibc aborts on buffer overflow.
